subtype: Approach: weigh job security against integrity in a values list [Thinking]
passage:
"You've been staring at that page for an hour," said Jomon's brother, Sachin, setting down two teacups.

"It's a list. Left side: my salary, the loan instalment, Amma's medicines. Right side: my name, the risk if the audit catches it, and whether I can look at myself."

"What did the manager ask, exactly?"

"To mark the delivery as received before the truck even came. I'd be signing a false line."

"And the left side?"

"Heavy. But if I sign and it comes out, I lose the job anyway, and my name with it."

"So?"

"So I say no tomorrow. And tonight I update my CV, just in case." Jomon tore his page in half and set the CV half on the laptop.

qa.q: What did the manager ask Jomon to do?
qa.a: To mark the delivery as received before the truck even came.

qa.q: What is Jomon feeling as he weighs the two sides of the list?
qa.a: Jomon feels torn and anxious about the salary and loan on one side, but the list leaves him more certain that his self-respect and name matter too.

qa.q: What could Jomon say to the manager to make the refusal easier to hear, and why?
qa.a: Jomon could offer to record the delivery honestly on the day it arrives, because it meets the manager's need for an accurate record without a false line.

qa.q: How might Sachin see Jomon's plan to refuse and update the CV?
qa.a: Sachin may feel relieved and proud that Jomon is not acting rashly, since the CV shows the refusal comes with a backup.

grounding: An employee lists what is at stake on each side, decides to refuse, and prepares a job-market backup.

subtype: Approach: seek a witness or written instruction [Action]
passage:
Subject: Confirming your request about the invoice date

Dear Pallavi,

Thank you for speaking with me this afternoon. To make sure I have understood: you asked me to change the date on the supplier's invoice to last month so that it shows in this quarter's figures.

I'm not comfortable altering the date on a document. Could you please confirm in writing whether you want me to do this, and who will approve it? Until I hear from you, I will file the invoice with its actual date and add a note about the timing. I have copied Anjum from Accounts so that we all have the same record.

Regards,
Francis

Reply, next morning: "Leave it as it is. I'll sort the timing another way."

qa.q: Whom did Francis copy on the email?
qa.a: Anjum from Accounts.

qa.q: What does Francis's wording, 'I'm not comfortable', suggest about how Francis feels?
qa.a: It suggests Francis is uneasy and polite but firm, not wanting to fight while still refusing to change a document.

qa.q: If Pallavi had insisted in writing, what could Francis do next, and why?
qa.a: Francis could take the written request to a senior person or the ethics contact, because the record shows what was asked and protects Francis from being blamed.

qa.q: How might Pallavi feel on reading the email?
qa.a: Pallavi may feel caught off guard and realise the request now has a paper trail, which likely prompts a rethink about the reply.

grounding: An employee emails the boss to summarise the request and ask for written confirmation, creating a clear record of responsibility.

subtype: Approach: prepare an exit plan if the culture will not change [Revision]
passage:
Day 2. The manager had asked Wasim again to shave the numbers on the vendor sheet, third time in a month, this time with a smile and a hint about his appraisal. Wasim went home and thought: refusing is right, but it won't change how this place works. On Sunday he updated his CV.

Day 10. He messaged three former classmates, asking without drama what their firms were like. Hansa replied within the hour: her company had a proper compliance team, and there was an opening in the finance unit. She sent the link.

Day 31. Wasim still went to work, still refused when asked. That Friday, though, he had an interview at Hansa's company, wearing the shirt he kept for occasions.

qa.q: How many times had the manager asked Wasim to shave the numbers by Day 2?
qa.a: It was the third time in a month.

qa.q: What was Wasim thinking when he updated his CV that Sunday?
qa.a: Wasim felt that refusing was right but would not change the workplace, so he wanted a way out while staying firm.

qa.q: What other step could Wasim take while he keeps working there, and why?
qa.a: He could keep a dated note of each request and know who to approach if pressure grows, because widening his options does not remove the need to stay protected now.

qa.q: How might Hansa see Wasim's message asking about her company?
qa.a: Hansa may see an old classmate who trusted her enough to ask honestly, and be glad to point out a good opening.

grounding: After repeated pressure, an employee updates the CV, contacts classmates and looks for better workplaces while still refusing.

passage:
I'm Imran, and I sit two desks from Jagdish, our junior auditor. On Tuesday I saw him frown at his screen for a long time. He'd noticed the same vendor being paid again and again, with nothing in the delivery register to match.

I expected him to blurt out a conclusion. Instead he murmured, half to himself, "Could be a filing gap. Could be another receiving log. What would tell error from wrongdoing? Delivery notes, a purchase order, an approval trail." He wrote three words on a sticky note and went to check the archive room.

I can't say what he was feeling. He looked calm, though he chewed his pen a lot. I just know he didn't call anybody a thief that day.

qa.q: Where did Jagdish go after writing on the sticky note?
qa.a: He went to check the archive room.

qa.q: What might Jagdish have been feeling as he chewed his pen while checking the vendor payments?
qa.a: He may have been uneasy or cautious, though Imran admits he only looked calm and cannot be sure.

qa.q: What else could Jagdish do if the archive room had no papers, and why?
qa.a: He could ask the receiving staff whether deliveries were logged somewhere else, because a missing record has innocent explanations too and each answer narrows the picture.

qa.q: How does Imran see Jagdish's caution compared with rushing to conclude?
qa.a: Imran expected a hasty accusation and instead saw restraint, which protects people who may turn out to be innocent.

grounding: An auditor notices repeated vendor payments without delivery records and reasons about alternative explanations before judging.

subtype: Approach: check the company whistleblower policy and legal protection [Action]
passage:
Note on Asif, audit trainee, written by Binita, audit supervisor.

Asif came to me on Wednesday and asked only where the whistleblower policy was kept. I gave him the printed copy and the general leaflet on legal protections, and did not ask why. Over an hour I watched him read both, underlining which office gets a report and what stays private. He asked whether the compliance officer sits outside the audit line, and I said yes.

He then closed the folder and said he would decide by Friday. I told him I was happy to talk if he wanted, but that he need not tell me the details. He seems anxious, but he chose to learn the channels before acting.

qa.q: What did Asif ask Binita about first?
qa.a: Asif asked only where the whistleblower policy was kept.

qa.q: How does Asif seem to be feeling as he reads and underlines the pages?
qa.a: Asif seems anxious but careful, wanting to be sure the channel and confidentiality are safe before acting.

qa.q: What could Asif do if the policy left a question unanswered, and why?
qa.a: Asif could ask the compliance office how a report is handled, because the people who run the channel can explain confidentiality better than guesses can.

qa.q: How might Binita's response make Asif's decision easier?
qa.a: Binita gave the materials and offered to talk without demanding details, so Asif can think freely without feeling watched or pressured.

grounding: A trainee reads the internal policy and general legal protections and considers who receives a report and what stays private.

subtype: Approach: confront the colleague in anger [Pitfall]
passage:
I was three desks away when Sahil found out about the payments. He read the spreadsheet, went white, then stormed across the open office and said loudly to Rohit, "You've been cooking these numbers, haven't you?"

Everyone stopped typing. Rohit said nothing, just looked at the floor. Over lunch, though, I noticed his monitor was dark and his drive folder was almost empty. By evening two teammates had stopped speaking to Sahil, and one whispered that he had ruined someone's career on a hunch.

I'm Madhuri. I can't tell whether Sahil was furious or scared, maybe both. I do know that a quiet report with the files intact would have been much harder to brush off.

qa.q: What happened to Rohit's drive folder by lunch?
qa.a: It was almost empty, and his monitor was dark.

qa.q: What might Sahil have been feeling when he crossed the office to speak to Rohit?
qa.a: Sahil was probably angry and shocked, though Madhuri admits it might also have been fear, which is why the outburst came so fast.

qa.q: What could Sahil have done instead of confronting Rohit, and why would it work better?
qa.a: Sahil could have saved a copy of what he found and taken it privately to the right person, because the evidence would stay intact and no one would be warned.

qa.q: How might Rohit have felt in the open office?
qa.a: Rohit likely felt exposed and cornered, with everyone watching, which makes hiding the files a frightened first move rather than a considered one.

grounding: Upset by a discovery, a person accuses a colleague in an open office, files vanish and the team turns hostile.

subtype: Approach: consult a mentor or lawyer for confidential guidance [Action]
passage:
Hemant worked as a junior auditor at the cooperative bank in the market town, and he could not sleep after seeing the loan register. On Sunday he took the bus to see Tarun sir, a senior at the federation office, who sat outside the branch's reporting line and would keep quiet. They talked on the verandah over tea.

A week later, Hemant met an advocate he had known since college, in a small office above the cloth shop. The advocate listened to the whole account and set out the possible options and what each might cost him. He asked Hemant to note dates and to tell nobody in the branch yet.

Hemant rode home with a page of notes and a steadier chest.

qa.q: Where did Hemant meet the advocate?
qa.a: In a small office above the cloth shop.

qa.q: What was Hemant feeling on the bus to see Tarun sir?
qa.a: Hemant felt uneasy and worried, since he could not sleep and needed a trusted person outside his own line to talk to.

qa.q: If the advocate had been busy, what else could Hemant do, and why?
qa.a: Hemant could speak again with Tarun sir about who else could advise him in confidence, because keeping the circle small guards against the matter spreading.

qa.q: How might Tarun sir see Hemant's coming to him first?
qa.a: Tarun sir may feel trusted and want to respond carefully, knowing a young clerk has placed a heavy concern in his hands.

grounding: An auditor consults a senior mentor outside the reporting line and an advocate confidentially to weigh options and risks.

subtype: Approach: do nothing because it is not my job [Pitfall]
passage:
Chidi saw the mismatch on his second week at the firm in Manchester: three payments that did not line up with the delivery sheets. He mentioned it to Jamal, the analyst at the next desk, who shrugged. "Someone above us must have seen it. It isn't our job."

Chidi nodded, relieved. Raising it might make him look like a rookie hunting for trouble, and his probation review was coming. He turned back to his own work.

Six months later the same gap had grown into a dozen entries. When the external team asked who had checked the sheets, Chidi's initials were on the working papers. Jamal said he'd assumed Chidi had handled it, and Chidi realised they had each thought the other would speak.

qa.q: What did Jamal say when Chidi mentioned the payments?
qa.a: Jamal said that someone above them must have seen it and that it was not their job.

qa.q: Why did Chidi feel relieved after Jamal's answer?
qa.a: Chidi was worried about looking like a rookie before his probation review, so being told it was not his job excused him from the risk.

qa.q: What could Chidi have done in the second week instead, and why?
qa.a: Chidi could have quietly asked his supervisor whether the payments were already known, because a simple question checks the assumption without accusing anyone.

qa.q: How does Jamal see the situation when the external team asks questions?
qa.a: Jamal thought Chidi had handled it, so Jamal sees a shared silence in which each person assumed someone else was responsible.

grounding: A person tells themselves the problem is not their job and others must know, and the problem grows.

subtype: Approach: pre-mortem on retaliation and support [Thinking]
passage:
Esther sat cross-legged on the sofa in Accra while her flatmate Ada made tea. "Say it aloud," Ada said. "What is the worst that happens if you report the false expense claims?"

"They freeze me out," Esther said slowly. "My manager gives me a bad review. Lunch alone. Someone whispers that I am not a team player."

"Then what?"

"Then I keep copies of my own appraisals and targets, in my own folder. I save the HR contact's number. And I keep three months of salary untouched, just in case." She wrote the list down.

"Do you still want to report it?"

Esther exhaled. "Yes. But now I know what to do if it goes badly."

qa.q: What did Esther plan to keep in her own folder?
qa.a: Copies of her own appraisals and targets.

qa.q: How does Esther feel when she says the worst might be a freeze-out and lunch alone?
qa.a: Esther feels anxious and a little sad about being isolated, but naming it lets her face it without panic.

qa.q: What else could Esther add to her plan, and why?
qa.a: Esther could name one trusted colleague or friend to check in during the hard weeks, because support outside the office makes isolation easier to bear. 🤍

qa.q: How does Ada help Esther see the plan?
qa.a: Ada asks calm questions rather than giving orders, so Esther can find her own answers and feel supported by a flatmate who takes the fear seriously.

grounding: Esther imagines the report going badly and plans with copies of records, an HR contact and savings, so she can act with eyes open.

subtype: Approach: file a factual written report through the proper channel [Action]
passage:
Thursday, 8 pm. Sent it today. It took three drafts because I kept adding adjectives and then deleting them.

What I finally wrote to Pankaj, the compliance officer: the dates of the six payments, the amounts, the invoice numbers and the folder references where the papers sit. I said what I had checked and what I had not been able to check. I did not say who I thought was responsible, and I did not guess at reasons. Just facts someone else can open and verify.

Hands were cold when I pressed send. Pankaj replied within the hour, confirming receipt and saying the matter will be handled through the proper process. Now I wait, and try not to check my email every ten minutes. Wasim

qa.q: To whom did Wasim send the report?
qa.a: To Pankaj, the compliance officer.

qa.q: How was Wasim feeling when pressing send, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Wasim was nervous, shown by cold hands and the urge to check email every ten minutes.

qa.q: What could Wasim do while waiting for the investigation, and why?
qa.a: Wasim could keep working normally and keep a copy of what was sent, because a calm routine and a record protect against both worry and misunderstanding.

qa.q: How might Pankaj see a report written with only dates and references?
qa.a: Pankaj can check each item independently and start work at once, because nothing in the report needs to be argued about first.

grounding: Wasim submits a concise report of dates, amounts and references to the compliance officer, leaving out accusations.
